pr_title: FEAT / Bitsandbytes: Add `dequantize` API for bitsandbytes quantized models
pr_body:
# What does this PR do?

Fixes https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/30177

This PR adds a new feature `dequantize` in order to de-quantize models for interesting usecases such as the one described in #30177 

The API is very simple:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, BitsAndBytesConfig, AutoTokenizer

model_id = "facebook/opt-125m"

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, quantization_config=BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True))
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)

model.dequantize()

text = tokenizer("Hello my name is", return_tensors="pt").to(0)

out = model.generate(**text)
print(tokenizer.decode(out[0]))
```

Users just need to make sure they have enough GPU RAM in order to store the unquantized model, otherwise they might face unexpected behaviour

Added the support for 4-bit / 8-bit models and nice tests + docs to educate users on how to use this new API.

cc @amyeroberts @SunMarc

issue_context.title: Load nf4 weights/model in bfloat16
issue_context.body:
### Feature request

Allow quantized models to be loaded (upcasted) to bfloat16.

### Motivation

1. The big benefit of QLoRA is being able to fine-tune on less VRAM AND with much less time than full fine-tuning.
2. Adding in rsLoRA, initiating LoRA adapters to minimise quanting error,  and training norm and embedding layers gets performance close to full fine-tuning.

HOWEVER, there's a catch that it's not possible to get back to a bf16 model (yes, it's possible to merge to 4-bit, but this hurts accuracy, and there's no way to upcast either). See [this issue](https://github.com/huggingface/peft/pull/851).


### Your contribution

BEST approach:
- Allow a type of merge where a quantized base model is merged with LoRA weights to form a 16 bit (float16 or bfloat16) model. [Obviously this will take more RAM or VRAM, so may not suit certain users, but it is best for quality].

HACKY but sufficient approach:
- Simply allow a quantized model (i.e. saved like [this](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/26037)] to be loaded in bfloat 16. If that's possible, then the following flow would work:
1. Fine tune a model with QLoRA (ideally making norms and embeds trainable). [initialise the adapters to minimise quanting error]
2. Save adapters.
3. Unload the adapters and save the nf4 base model (ideally including the trained norms and embeds)
4. Re-load the nf4 base model, but upcasted to bfloat16.
5. Apply the adapter
6. Merge the adapter to the base model
7. This should result in a highly accurate final model.

Everything 1-7 is possible already except for step 4. However, step 4 is done in unsloth, see [here](https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth/issues/195), so should be fairly easy.

[Side note - I'm unsure whether bnb quants the norm and embed layers, or just the linear layers?]

for the step 4-, why users couldn't simply load again the base model but directly in bf16 ? What would be the benefit of un-quantizing on the fly a 4bit model vs loading it directly in 16bit ? Is it to preserve the quantization error?

> for the step 4-, why users couldn't simply load again the base model but directly in bf16 ? What would be the benefit of un-quantizing on the fly a 4bit model vs loading it directly in 16bit ? Is it to preserve the quantization error?

Yeah, a base bf16 model will have slightly different weights than a quantized and then dequantized bf16 model. This makes a performance difference when applying and merging the 16 bit adapters on top.

review_comments:
One general comment, if instead you could have a private method `_dequantize_and_replace`, which handles the recursion, you don't need to return `has_been_replaced` here. When someone calls `dequantize_and_replace`, I don't think `has_been_replaced` is ever used and could be confusing e.g.: 

```
# This is just dequantize_and_replace from before
def _dequantize_and_replace(
    model,
    modules_to_not_convert=None,
    current_key_name=None,
    quantization_config=None,
    has_been_replaced=False,
):
    ...
    return model, has_been_replaced

def dequantize_and_replace(
    model,
    modules_to_not_convert=None,
    current_key_name=None,
    quantization_config=None,
    has_been_replaced=False,
):
    model, has_been_replaced = _dequantize_and_replace(...)
    return model 
```
